assertions.name: coordination_is_body_order_tower_not_single_graph
assertions.source: chain and Borromean are COMPLEMENTARY at different orders — chain M_2=1>0 Borromean (pairwise), Borromean M_3=1>0 chain (triple) — with equal tower rank (1=1). ⇒ max-binding does NOT select a single 'richest-tower' graph (refuted); the coordination is the body-order tower B=Σ_n B_n, each M_n from its own Brunnian-n sub-link. Chain undercount = missing M_3.

description: Coordination graph M_n(K) (qou-v0yw): tests a max-binding 'richest Milnor tower' selection principle and REFUTES it — the reducible chain (M_2=1, M_3=0) and the Brunnian Borromean (M_2=0, M_3=1) have EQUAL tower rank; the Borromean trades pairwise for the irreducible triple. Correct reading: the coordination is a body-order TOWER (ledger §0), not one graph — M_2 from pairwise links, M_3 from Borromean triples, each order using its own Brunnian-n sub-link. Explains #3545 Part 8's chain undercount (a pure chain is missing M_3). Reframes qou-v0yw as a per-order sub-link COUNTING problem (not single-graph selection); the counts + M_n→w_n weights stay OPEN. Scope-(a), reuses #3545 machinery, no fit, no wiring.
